<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `current_user (literal, 34 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e5899a67d641aed9387707511bbbbe6a64d25c5b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6847343d94af3ef6ae58ea7cf2b7eefd1ca1dd16` — the merge of head `0e51b65d0952e5e1be69a5bd05f215722e2648c9` into base `e5899a67d641aed9387707511bbbbe6a64d25c5b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6847343d94af3ef6ae58ea7cf2b7eefd1ca1dd16 && git checkout 6847343d94af3ef6ae58ea7cf2b7eefd1ca1dd16
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e5899a67d641aed9387707511bbbbe6a64d25c5b 0e51b65d0952e5e1be69a5bd05f215722e2648c9 && git checkout -B drift-repro e5899a67d641aed9387707511bbbbe6a64d25c5b && git merge --no-ff 0e51b65d0952e5e1be69a5bd05f215722e2648c9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e5899a67d641aed9387707511bbbbe6a64d25c5b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e5899a67d641aed9387707511bbbbe6a64d25c5b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0e51b65d0952e5e1be69a5bd05f215722e2648c9`
Local-runs: none

PR #22730 (card #22677), read at 2026-10-10T21:05Z. Inputs: the card's body and every comment (triage `6097216432`, unlock `6097731915`, seat 2's serial note, the claim `6101461546`, both dev reports, the seat order `6102049574`, the ACCEPT `6102086025`); #22565's landing note `6096002029` and #22636's body; PR #22674's diff; PR #22730's body, file list and net diff against the merge base `762db996ad` (9 files, +268 / -48); the engine and trigger sources on `origin/main`; the check-runs on this head. Read-only: `git fetch` into `refs/pm/pr-22730`, `git show` / `git diff`, and REST GETs. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**The refused set — `record` leaves `ENGINE_BOUND_ROOTS` and is bound by `flowCelEntrances`' new `handed` set. Right**, checked entrance by entrance against the engine on `main` after PR #22674 (`seedRunVariables` binds `context.record` as `record` and nothing else does; `celScope` has no `record` slot):

- `record_change` — `resolveFlowTriggerKind` answers it only for a string `config.triggerType` starting `record-`; `deriveTriggerBinding` routes that kind to the record-change trigger, which hands `record: isolatedRecord`. **A start `config.objectName` alone resolves to no kind, binds to no trigger and hands no record** (`deriveTriggerBinding` reads `objectName` only inside the `record_change` arm; the API run door and the schedule hand none). The dev's reading is right, and the `objectName`-alone refusal is pinned. The array-form `triggerType` resolves to no kind in the spec resolver, and the engine's route for it is a bind-time refusal, so it hands none either: right.
- `time_relative` — `config.timeRelative` object; the sweep hands each matched row as `record`. Right.
- `api` — `type: 'api'` or `triggerType: 'api'` at the resolver's lowest precedence; `trigger-api` hands `record: payload`. Right, and the flow is also opened (unchanged), so `record` is bound there and nothing is judged.
- `type: 'flow'` action — `dispatchFlowAction` always calls `automation.execute(target, { record, ... })` with `loadActionSubjectRecord`'s `record`: the loaded row, or `{}` carrying at most the `id`. `seedRunVariables`' `if (context?.record)` is truthy on `{}`, so an object-less action binds `record` (plus `id`). Right, both actions and `objects[].actions[]` are read.
- `map` — handed only with a `config.itemObject`; `map-node.ts` hands an id-bearing item as the child's `record`, else the parent's context record. Without `itemObject` the child is opened (unchanged), so `record` is never falsely refused in a `map` child. Residual, not a defect: a `map` with `itemObject` whose items carry no `id` under a record-less parent is a false pass, never a false refusal, and `itemObject` asserts the items are records. Consistent with triage's "a `map`".
- `subflow` / `map` child of a handed parent — both executors spread `...context` into the child, record included; `handed` propagates over the parent edges to a fixpoint. A parent's `record` VARIABLE is not handed (the child gets context, not variables): right, and pinned red.
- a declared `record` variable or `assignment` target — `collectFlowVariableNames` rows 1 and 7. Right (runtime values it only with an input or `defaultValue`: the judge-wide #22565 design, acceptance note 2).

**`previous` kept as an engine root. Right**: `seedRunVariables` sets `variables.set('previous', context?.previous ?? null)` on every run.

**The runtime gate's S stand-down still covers `record`. Right**: `validate-expressions.ts` and `runtime-gate.ts` are untouched; a `runtimeWriteType` write still gets `perWriteSnapshotEntrance()`, whose `openedBy` makes the scope unprovable, so no root is judged there, `record` included. Pinned (the gate passes `record.status` on a flow write while `validate` refuses it on the same flow). **No other verdict moved**: the diff changes the bound set, adds the `handed` read, hoists `resolveFlowTriggerKind` into `kind` (same `api` test), and adds a `record`-specific message; the `opened` reasons, the node-type stand-downs and the generic message's shape are unchanged apart from its corrected closing clause.

**The refusal text. Right**: a `record` read names the root, the `Unknown variable: record` fault, the entrances that would hand one, the variable-name / `vars` remedy #22642 prescribes, and the entrance remedy. No tracker number in the runtime string.

**The D3 entry `flow-cel-unbound-root-refused`. Right**: the diff touches `reason` only (the FROM/TO the PR body quotes, verbatim), no other key; `registry.ts` carries the same 4-line change and the registry block equals the entry block after indentation (normalised compare at the head). `check:migration-registry` runs in `Lint & Repo Gates`, in progress at this reading; the dev's run reports the registry current.

**Fixtures.** 9 `validate-expressions.test.ts` start nodes and the `lint-flow-patterns` `valueFlow` gain a `record-*` trigger (the latter declares `task` so the judgment stays live); 3 of #22565's own pins move `record` to a record-triggered control. Text-only, and each reads `record.X` with no entrance, so the census is coherent. The #4811 comment correction is accurate.

**Reach.** 0 newly refused over `examples/**` (35 flows, 14 reading `record`), `platform-objects` (0) and hotcrm `1d7148b` (32 / 14), with a positive control. Taken as read; consistent with #22642's census.

**Check-runs on this head, at this reading.** Concluded green: Build Core, Dogfood Regression Gate (1/3), Dogfood Verify CLI, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, the four claim and closing guards, Check PR Size, Auto Label, filter. Concluded red: Check Changeset (twice) — its log names exactly `.changeset/22565-flow-cel-unbound-root-refused.md` and `.changeset/22642-flow-cel-record-binding.md` under the foreign-changeset rule, the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class, while its `check-adr-0087-registration` step passes with the `already-registered` notice and its `check-changeset-no-major` step passes (pre mode, level axis OK). Red by design, advisory (not one of the seven required contexts), and this record is the class's confirmation. Still running: Lint & Repo Gates, Test Core (1–6), Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Regression Gate (2/3, 3/3). Skipped: Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke. Judged on the concluded ones; the pre-queue step still needs the required set green.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/22677-flow-cel-record-entrance.md`: `'@objectstack/lint': major`. **Admissible and consistent**: `.changeset/pre.json` is `mode: pre`, tag `next`, so the no-major guard stands aside (its CI step says so on this changeset), the fixed group is already majored by the pending spec `major`, and the product is `18.0.0-next.N` either way. It matches #22565's note for the same rule and package (`major`), while #22642's twin took `minor` under the launch-window convention; in the window the level is not the carrier, and this note carries the breaking-ness itself: `**BREAKING**`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` (right — an accept-set narrowing of `objectstack validate`'s `expression-invalid` rule), the FROM → TO table and the one-line fix.

`adr-0087: not-required (already-registered flow-cel-unbound-root-refused, flow-cel-record-variables-alias-retired)`. **Right, no new D3 entry owed**: both ids resolve at the head and at the merge base (PR #22674's merge `243dd3c625` is an ancestor of `762db996ad`); neither has shipped (protocol 18 pending, `@objectstack/spec` at 17.7.0). The surface this PR narrows — a `record` read on a flow no entrance hands a record — is a root the flow does not bind, which is `flow-cel-unbound-root-refused`'s surface, and its corrected `reason` now says so; the run-time half and the author's rewrite (variable name or `vars.X`) are `flow-cel-record-variables-alias-retired`'s FROM → TO. Correcting two unreleased entries in place is the right route; a third entry would duplicate them in the upgrade guide.

### ③ Boundary flags

**DELIBERATE CORRECTION class — confirmed, both notes, sentence by sentence.** `check-empty-changeset` names exactly these two files and nothing else; neither is restored from the base, and this record confirms each correction as true at this head:

`.changeset/22565-flow-cel-unbound-root-refused.md` (net diff 4 / 3, three hunks, nothing else moved):
1. Why paragraph — before: "the trigger record's fields flattened beside them, and `record`, `previous`, `vars` and `current_user` bound by the engine." After: "the trigger record's fields flattened beside them, `record` bound to the record the run was handed (where an entrance hands it one), and `previous`, `vars` and `current_user` bound by the engine." **Confirmed**: that is `seedRunVariables` on `main`.
2. What is refused, first bullet — before: "the engine's roots: `record`, `previous`, `vars`, `current_user`;". After: "the engine's roots: `previous`, `vars`, `current_user`;" plus the new bullet "`record`, where an entrance the stack declares hands the flow a record — a record trigger (a `record-*` `triggerType`), a time-relative sweep, the inbound hook, a `type: 'flow'` action, a `map` node with an `itemObject`, or a `subflow` / `map` parent handed one — or where the flow binds a variable named `record`;". **Confirmed**: it is the `handed` set and the variable binding, exactly as the judge reads them.
3. Who is affected — before: "every root those flows read is an engine root, a binding of the flow's own or a field of its trigger object." After: "every root those flows read is an engine root, `record` on a flow an entrance hands a record, a binding of the flow's own or a field of its trigger object." **Confirmed**: the reach shows every `record`-reading example flow is handed one.

`.changeset/22642-flow-cel-record-binding.md` (net diff 1 / 1, the one sentence, nothing else moved, as the seat order `6102049574` set): before: "`objectstack validate` does not refuse such a `record` read yet; the run fails it, naming the root and the source." After: "`objectstack validate` refuses such a `record` read too, naming the root (see `@objectstack/lint`'s note)." **Confirmed**: at this head `validate` refuses it as `expression-invalid`, `error`, naming `record`; the lint note carries the stand-downs (a flow the reader cannot prove, and the runtime publish gate until #22636).

**Dev deviations the ACCEPT records — each judged:**
- "a trigger object" read as the record trigger (`record_change`), measured on `deriveTriggerBinding`: **right** against triage's direction `6097216432`; the direction's "a trigger object" is what hands a row only through a `record-*` trigger, and the nine fixture edits plus the `objectName`-alone pin follow from it.
- The `metadata-protocol` suite and the CLI flow files ran on the pre-merge tree: acceptable, the merge of `762db996ad` touched neither the judge nor those packages' flow paths and the judge blob is identical at the head; Test Core on this head is the second reading.
- hotcrm measured at `1d7148b` while the #22565 note cites `f0afcbda07`: each note names its own tree and commit; acceptable.
- This PR's own 22677 note dropped its closing line in the patch round, and the PR-context guards were re-run on the refreshed body: both within the claim's surface; acceptable.
- The CLI closure build under the verify lock and the worktree cleanup: process notes, nothing to judge.

**Out-of-scope findings:**
- The `opened`-set gap (a `record-*` trigger with no start `config.objectName` registers its hook with `object: binding.object` undefined, so it fires on any object's write, while `flowCelEntrances` opens only on a named, undeclared `objectName`): a real inference, pre-existing from #22565's `opened` logic and untouched by this PR; its consequence is a possible false refusal of a bare field root on a degenerate authoring shape, not a false pass of `record`. The trigger-readiness rule refuses only a mismatched `objectName`, not an absent one, so the shape reaches `validate`. Carrier #22636 is the right one (same judge, widens the same reader); the seat's commitment to note it there at landing is held to.
- A declared `record` variable binds at the build door as every declared variable does: #22565's judge-wide design, an acceptance note, nothing owed here.

**The two open questions:**
- Q1, answered A: the one-sentence correction is in the diff, confirmed above. Answered.
- Q2, answered A (leave "none of these roots ever evaluated in a flow" in the #22565 note's ledger bullet, the D3 `reason` and the registry): **accepted, not escalated.** The clause is imprecise for `record` on 17.x, but the behaviour change it would describe is carried, with its FROM → TO, by `flow-cel-record-variables-alias-retired`, which this PR's disposition names beside the unbound-root entry; an upgrading reader who greps `record` lands on that entry. Amending the clause would be a second text-only edit outside triage's "the record-bound sentence" scope, and it is not required for the ledger to be coherent.

**Nothing else flagged**: no governed surface in the file list, no `validate-expressions.ts` change, no example changed, no registry entry added, no tracker number in a runtime string.
